fact_check_rounds.label: Round 1: the 40 profiled plants (after the parallel list audit)
Round 2: confirming round, all 47 profiled plants, checkers rotated (after the sweep)
Round 3: the 21 profiles added in the last waves (profilers G, H, I and J)
Base-record sample: 25 closure-3 base records (reported separately; not a profile round)

miss_rate.value: 45/163 = 27.6% (blind re-audit, verified); up to 61/179 = 34.1% if the 16 unsettled candidates are real
miss_rate.note: Second blind audit (two independent auditors, 2026-11-16) against the list after three closure passes. The auditors' 225 in-definition rows: 153 matched 125 ledger plants (23 plants were found more than once), 72 did not match. Of the 125, 117 are included and 8 are excluded with sourced reasons (closed, office, distribution or assembly-only sites); the 8 leave the count. Of the 72, one was already in the ledger (Ashland, WI). Two plant-finders checked the other 71: 46 new base (45 in definition; Pemberton FL is unsettled), 10 excluded (out of vertical, offices, dealers, fabrication contracted out), 15 unverified. Miss rate = 45 / (117 + 1 + 45). All 46 are now in the ledger as base records; merging them does not lower the measured rate. Misses cluster in CONEXPO-CON/AGG exhibitors the EPA-registry closure passes never reached. Two verified misses rank inside the top 40 by the profiling key with counted welder postings (both profiled afterwards): Fecon, Lebanon OH (rank 11; three undated own-board welder postings; boundary, forestry mulching attachments) and General Steel & Supply (Fisher Industries), Dickinson ND (rank 23; two dated postings with a sign-on bonus; site tie inferred under the campus rule).

known_limits: Partial: the blind re-audit's verified miss rate is 27.6%, over the 20% done threshold. Crusher, screen and asphalt-plant makers look close to complete; small attachment and bucket makers, small conveyor and aggregate fabricators, and Tier 1 weldment shops are not.

The two verified misses that ranked in the top 40 with counted postings were profiled afterwards: Fecon, Lebanon OH, 76 High (three undated welder postings open at once; boundary, forestry mulching attachments) and General Steel & Supply (Fisher Industries), Dickinson ND, 28 Low under the strict campus rule (75 High if a 2021 source placing both fabrication facilities on its Energy Drive campus is accepted). The top 40 is now fully profiled.

About 155 EPA registry rows and named leads from closure remain unverified, plus 15 re-audit candidates and leads such as Tricon's other plants, Power Curbers' Cedar Falls and McHenry plants, HitchDoc's Kwik-Way Sioux Falls plant and Amerequip's New Holstein plants.

Fact-check: round 1 11.4%; round 2 (all 47 profiles, rotated) 3.3%; round 3 (the 21 newest profiles) 16/417 = 3.8% overall, but 7.3% for profiler I's seven (12.8% counting untrimmed sibling rows). All corrections applied. The round-3 sweep of compound-value clauses was run only on the newest profiles. A separate sample of 25 closure base records found 1.5%.

Brookville Equipment, Brookville PA scores 63 Medium under the written campus rule: the flat car's size is a company-level fact and a second Brookville site (service and rebuilds) is 1.3 km away. If the rebuild shop is ruled not a production site, it is 83 High.

Material scores 0 on 59 of 68 profiled plants: mining and construction sources rarely state a welded part's size or weight, and payloads, bucket capacities and machine classes do not count as part sizes.

Paladin Dexter MI is profiled as a boundary plant: no Paladin page says what it builds, and EPA's facility name (Sweepster-Harley Attachments) points to sweeper and broom attachments, which would exclude it under the M-B New Holstein ruling.
Only 68 of 352 included plants are profiled; base records carry no score.
Auditor B could see file names (not contents) in the shared scratchpad during the re-audit, so its blindness is slightly weaker than auditor A's.
